Fractions and Thresholds.q: To impeach a federal official, the House of Representatives must vote by what margin?
Fractions and Thresholds.e: A simple majority impeaches. Conviction in the Senate is the higher bar.

Fractions and Thresholds.q: To convict and remove an impeached official, the Senate must vote by what margin?
Fractions and Thresholds.e: Two-thirds of senators present. The House charges by majority; the Senate removes by two-thirds.

Fractions and Thresholds.q: For Congress to propose a constitutional amendment, what vote is required?
Fractions and Thresholds.e: Two-thirds of both the House and the Senate.

Fractions and Thresholds.q: How many states must ratify a proposed constitutional amendment?
Fractions and Thresholds.e: Three-fourths. Two-thirds belongs to the proposal stage; three-fourths to ratification.

Fractions and Thresholds.q: Under the alternative route in Article V, an amendment may be proposed by a convention called by
Fractions and Thresholds.e: Two-thirds of state legislatures can call a convention. This route has never been used.

Fractions and Thresholds.q: To override a presidential veto, Congress must vote by what margin?
To ratify a treaty, the Senate must vote by what margin?
Fractions and Thresholds.e: Two-thirds of senators present. The House has no role in treaty ratification.

Fractions and Thresholds.q: To invoke cloture and end a filibuster on legislation, how many senators must vote yes?
To confirm a presidential nominee, the Senate votes by
Fractions and Thresholds.e: A simple majority confirms. Note the contrast with treaties, which take two-thirds.

Fractions and Thresholds.q: To expel one of its own members, a chamber of Congress must vote by what margin?
How many electoral votes are needed to win the presidency?
Fractions and Thresholds.e: 270 — a majority of the 538 electoral votes.

Fractions and Thresholds.q: The Three-Fifths Compromise counted three-fifths of a state’s enslaved population for purposes of
o: representation in the House and direct taxation
Fractions and Thresholds.e: Representation and taxation. Section 2 of the Fourteenth Amendment later replaced this formula.

Checks and Balances.q: Which branch has the power to declare war?
Checks and Balances.e: Congress declares war. The president is Commander in Chief and directs the military.

Checks and Balances.q: The Senate checks the president’s appointment power by
o: impeaching nominees before they take office
Checks and Balances.e: Advice and consent. The Senate confirms by simple majority.

Checks and Balances.q: The president checks Congress most directly through the power to
Checks and Balances.e: The veto. Congress can override it with two-thirds of both chambers.

Checks and Balances.q: The judicial branch checks the other two branches primarily through
Checks and Balances.e: Judicial review — declaring acts of Congress or the executive unconstitutional. Established in Marbury v. Madison (1803).

Checks and Balances.q: Which power allows the president to check the judicial branch?
Checks and Balances.e: The president nominates federal judges, subject to Senate confirmation. Presidents cannot overturn decisions or remove judges.

Checks and Balances.q: Which chamber brings impeachment charges, and which conducts the trial?
o: Both charge; the Supreme Court tries
House charges; the Supreme Court tries
Checks and Balances.e: The House impeaches; the Senate tries.

Checks and Balances.q: Who presides over the Senate trial when a president is impeached?
o: The Chief Justice of the United States
Checks and Balances.e: The Chief Justice presides when the president is tried. For other officials, the vice president or presiding officer does.

Checks and Balances.q: Congress can check the federal courts by
o: altering the size of the Supreme Court and the jurisdiction of lower courts
reversing Supreme Court rulings by majority vote
Checks and Balances.e: Congress sets the number of justices, creates lower courts, and defines their jurisdiction. It cannot reverse rulings by ordinary vote.

Checks and Balances.q: The president’s pardon power is a check on which branch?
Checks and Balances.e: A pardon sets aside the consequences of a criminal conviction, which checks the courts. It does not apply in cases of impeachment.

Checks and Balances.q: Congress’s most powerful ongoing check on the executive branch is its control over
Checks and Balances.e: The power of the purse. No federal money is spent without a congressional appropriation.

Checks and Balances.q: When the Supreme Court interprets the Constitution in a way Congress and the states disagree with, they may respond by
o: passing an ordinary statute overruling the decision
proposing and ratifying a constitutional amendment
voting to remove the justices by majority
Checks and Balances.e: Amending the Constitution is the formal route. An ordinary statute cannot override a constitutional ruling.

Checks and Balances.q: Which branch has the power to coin money and regulate its value?
Checks and Balances.e: Congress. Under the Articles of Confederation the states shared this power, which was a major weakness.

House vs. Senate.q: Where must all revenue bills originate?
House vs. Senate.e: The House — the chamber apportioned by population. The Senate may amend revenue bills but not originate them.

House vs. Senate.q: Which chamber allows unlimited debate unless cloture is invoked?
House vs. Senate.e: The Senate. That is what makes the filibuster possible; cloture takes 60 votes.

House vs. Senate.q: How long is a term in the House of Representatives?
House vs. Senate.e: Two years. Every House seat is up in every even-numbered year.

House vs. Senate.q: How long is a term in the Senate?
House vs. Senate.e: Six years, staggered so about one-third of the Senate is up each cycle.

House vs. Senate.q: How many members serve in the House of Representatives?
House vs. Senate.e: 435. Note that 538 is the number of electoral votes, not House seats.

House vs. Senate.q: How many members serve in the Senate?

House vs. Senate.e: The Senate, by a two-thirds vote.

House vs. Senate.q: Under the original Constitution, which chamber’s members were chosen by state legislatures rather than by voters?
House vs. Senate.e: The Senate. The Seventeenth Amendment (1913) replaced legislative selection with direct election.

o: Speaker of the House; vice president as president of the Senate
President pro tempore in the House; Speaker in the Senate
House vs. Senate.e: The Speaker leads the House. The vice president serves as president of the Senate and may break ties.

House vs. Senate.q: Seats in the House of Representatives are apportioned
House vs. Senate.e: By population — the Virginia Plan’s approach, preserved in the Great Compromise.

House vs. Senate.q: Seats in the Senate are apportioned
House vs. Senate.e: Equally — two per state, regardless of size. The New Jersey Plan’s approach, preserved in the Great Compromise.

o: 25 for the House, 30 for the Senate
21 for the House, 25 for the Senate
30 for the House, 35 for the Senate
House vs. Senate.e: 25 for the House, 30 for the Senate, 35 for the presidency.

House vs. Senate.q: If no candidate wins an Electoral College majority, which chamber chooses the president?
House vs. Senate.e: The House selects the president; the Senate separately selects the vice president.
